  • Racial Hierarchy and Nativism: Drawing from now-debunked racial theories, proponents argued that Asian immigration threatened the racial composition and supposed superiority of the nation. This was often couched in language about preserving "civilization" or maintaining demographic balance.

2. Employment Discrimination

Exclusion from certain professions, government jobs, and union membership was justified through:

  • Occupational Protectionism: Similar to immigration arguments, supporters claimed that restricting Asian access to skilled professions and unionized trades was necessary to maintain standards and protect incumbent workers. This was particularly prominent in agriculture, mining, and railroads in the western United States.
  • Perceived Loyalty Concerns: During periods of geopolitical tension (most notably WWII with Japanese Americans), supporters argued that employing people of Japanese descent posed national security risks.
